olivia: Ran a short nsys capture on the P4d repro (1k steps). Seeing a recurring ~5-7ms kernel spike that aligns with KV-cache misses.
sam: Can you share the timeline screenshot and whether this was hosted/dedicated?
olivia: Hosted. Screenshot in a sec. Quick note: the kernel label in the trace looks like cudnn_convolution or similar, but it only shows up on requests that trigger a ~1.2MB KV lookup.
mike: Hmm that sounds like the selector falling back to a dense matmul/conv path for small batch sizes because of tiling thresholds — we've seen that pattern before.
anya: Do we have per-request NVTX ranges around KV lookup/prefetch? Without them it's hard to map a specific request to kernels.
olivia: We currently emit per-batch NVTX ranges ("batch/forward" and generic "kernel/*"). No per-request spans; when I tried enabling per-request NVTX for a full capture it ballooned the trace (8x larger) so I turned it off.
sam: Could we sample per-request NVTX only for slow requests (latency > P95)? That would limit overhead and still give signals on outliers.
dev-bot: nsys job 1955001111 finished: duration=4.8s, kernels=342, nvtx_ranges=18, file=/tmp/nsys-1955.qd
mike: Proposal A: keep per-batch ranges, add a tiny id-only annotation at request boundary: nvtxRangePushA("req:abcd1234"); nvtxRangePop(); no heavy metadata. This lets us correlate without a huge trace size.
anya: If QPS is high even ID-only ranges are numerous. We should define a sampling strategy.
olivia: Proposal B: sample 1% of requests for full per-request spans + detailed KV markers (prefetch/start/finish). For the rest, emit the lightweight id-only tag. Full spans behind a sample flag gave good attribution in my quick run.
sam: Also instrument the kernel selector decisions: nvtxRangePushA("ks:fast_gemm") or nvtxRangePushA("ks:conv_fallback") so we can see which branch co-occurs with the long kernel.
mike: And add KV operation labels: "kv:lookup", "kv:miss_prefetch", "kv:apply". For detailed spans use nvtxRangePushEx to carry a numeric attribute for size (bytes).
olivia: Example pseudo-C I used: ```
nvtxRangePushA("req:abcd1234");
nvtxRangePushA("kv:lookup");
// do lookup
nvtxRangePop();
nvtxRangePushA("ks:fast_gemm");
// launch kernel
nvtxRangePop();
nvtxRangePop();
```
That ordering made mapping trivial but added ~20% trace overhead when enabled for 100% of requests.
anya: For naming, prefer short tokens with underscores: req_<short>, kv_<op>, ks_<decision>. Keep strings <= 32 chars to avoid NVTX payload bloat. Also use an 8-char hex shorthash of the request SHA1 for stability.
sam: For sampling controls, runtime can honor env var REDWOOD_NVTX_SAMPLE_RATE (e.g., 0.01) and decide per-request with a fast RNG. Devex can inject that for captures.
mike: If the selector is the culprit we should add a small micro-benchmark that reproduces the pattern (small B x large K) and try alternate tiling thresholds to see cost/latency tradeoffs.
anya: Action items: (olivia) add lightweight ks_* push/pop around selector; (mike) implement detailed kv_* spans behind sample flag; (anya) PR shortnames + max-length rule; (sam) run 10 nsys captures at sample rates [0,0.01,0.1] and compare kernel attribution.
olivia: I'll open a PR for the selector NVTX hooks and a short RFC for sampling semantics. I'll also drop the timeline link once the perfetto is uploaded.
mike: Good. If we can see the selector label adjacent to the long kernel it likely points to threshold tuning rather than model code.
olivia: Thanks — closing the loop here. We'll iterate on sample rate if trace sizes get unwieldy.
